clue.text: Spanish city, old one showing strength

parts.note: Vigo is a port city in Galicia, north-west Spain
following on from 'city', an old one is Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Someone praises a historic Spanish city for its robustness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'city': Ur is the classic crossword ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean physical energy and force.

clue.text: Thrilling sensation almost rushed before time

indicators.note: almost means the word for sensation loses its final letter

parts.note: a vibe is a feeling or sensation
ran means rushed or hurried

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a thrilling feeling that nearly made them hurry before the clock ran out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something vibrant is exciting and full of energy.

clue.text: A neat rug messed up close to fire getting warranty

indicators.note: messed up tells us the letters of the three words are jumbled
close to here means the very end of the word fire

explanation.surface: A tidy rug ruined by sitting near the fire leads to a claim on its warranty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' rearranges A NEAT RUG into GUARANTE; 'close to' supplies the E ending 'fire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a warranty is a formal promise covering a product's quality.

clue.text: Open article for Frenchman on Irish place

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a/an
Cork is a city and county in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: A Frenchman writes an article about a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to uncork a bottle is to open it by pulling its stopper.

clue.text: Volatile date embracing single fellow not appreciative of notes?

indicators.note: embracing means the rearranged letters wrap around the word for single
volatile, meaning unstable or changeable, tells us the letters of date are rearranged

parts.note: one means single

explanation.surface: An erratic date with a lone man who cannot appreciate music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile' gives TDEA; 'embracing' wraps it round the single, and 'notes?' hints at music rather than memos.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone unable to distinguish musical pitch gets nothing from the notes played.

clue.text: Common sense having to lower head for burden

indicators.note: to lower head means the first letter of the word is moved further down this down entry

parts.note: nous is British slang for common sense or practical intelligence

explanation.surface: Advice that common sense must bow its head under a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS (British informal for gumption) has its first letter N dropped one place, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an onus is a duty or responsibility one must bear.

clue.text: Speed up former exercise and revise diet

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
PE is physical education, i.e. exercise

indicators.note: revise means alter, so the letters of diet are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone wants to hurry their previous fitness routine and change what they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to expedite a process is to make it happen faster.

clue.text: In a high degree, regret raised money

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: so means very, to a high degree, as in so good
rue means regret

explanation.surface: Someone very sorry about the funds they collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole run SORUE upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: euros are the currency of much of the European Union.

clue.text: Funding that's new pocketed by one preparing for match

indicators.note: pocketed by means the letter for new is put inside the word for the person engaged

parts.note: a fiance is someone engaged and preparing for marriage, a match

explanation.surface: Fresh money pocketed by someone getting ready for a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport, but here it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: finance is money provided for a project or business.

clue.text: Bishop administered church subdivision

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ran means administered or managed

explanation.surface: A bishop ran a church, an offshoot of the main body.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a branch is a division of a larger organisation.

clue.text: Soft shoe by club for work with weights

parts.note: a pump is a light soft shoe, as for dancing or gym
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A slipper beside a golf club in the gym bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a nightclub or society; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: pumping iron is informal for weightlifting training.

clue.text: Locum beginning to tire entering hospital with noise

indicators.note: entering means that letter goes inside the word for hospital

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is a hospital

indicators.note: beginning to here means the first letter of the word tire

parts.note: din means loud noise

explanation.surface: A tired temporary doctor arrives at a noisy hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stand-in is a substitute, as a locum covers for an absent doctor.

clue.text: Friend half-heartedly taking in a review showing briskness

indicators.note: taking in means the shortened word wraps around the next pieces
half-heartedly means one of the two central letters of the word for friend is lost

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter
a crit is a critique or review

explanation.surface: A lukewarm friend reads a critique delivered with speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle Ls of ALLY, leaving ALY to hold A CRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: alacrity is eager promptness or speed.

clue.text: Old academic holding degree succeeded? Most likely

indicators.note: holding means the word for academic contains the next two letters

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
S is an abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Will an old professor with a doctorate inherit the post?
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from betting: a runner priced shorter than evens is the favourite, so very probable.

clue.text: Drivers organised to be in race, wonderful event

indicators.note: to be in means the drivers' body goes inside the word for race

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British organisation for motorists

explanation.surface: Motorists arranged to take part in a race and it went wonderfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring organisation; 'organised' describes the drivers as a body, not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a miracle is a marvellous, seemingly impossible happening.

clue.text: Carry rich pastry right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed from the word

parts.note: a torte is a rich cake or pastry

explanation.surface: Someone takes a rich cake straight off somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tote is to carry, as in a tote bag.

clue.text: Enter undetected current flat I rent in shabby state

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: in shabby state means the letters of the three words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tenant sneaks into a run-down flat they rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shabby state' rearranges FLAT I RENT into NFILTRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to infiltrate is to get into a place or group secretly.

clue.text: An attempt by province to celebrate that's very painful

parts.note: a go is an attempt, with A from the clue
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
to sing can mean to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Someone's effort to rejoice in their home region proves distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called the Province in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: agonising describes extreme suffering or anguish.

clue.text: Block bachelor, good man dividing reformed court

indicators.note: dividing means the next letters split the rearranged word
reformed means the letters of court are put together anew

parts.note: St, for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: An unmarried saint splits a reorganised court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' gives OURCT, which 'dividing' splits after its O; the good man is a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to obstruct is to stand in the way of or impede.

clue.text: A graduate pocketing almost nothing before start of year in Asia

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'A graduate pocketing almost nothing before start of year in Asia' builds A(ZER)BA + JAN but nothing gives the I of AZERBAIJAN; a word such as 'one' seems missing and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: A graduate pocketing almost nothing before start of year in Asia

clue.text: Think well of a very quiet car with concealed rear

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

indicators.note: with concealed rear means the last letter of the car is hidden away

parts.note: a Rover is a British make of car

explanation.surface: Someone admires a silent car with its back end out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to approve is to judge favourably.

clue.text: Argument backed by male, mean creature

indicators.note: backed means the word for argument is turned back to front

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A man joins a quarrel with a nasty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' is part of the definition: a worm is a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a worm is a weak, despicable person.

clue.text: Note Roman emperor and Roman goddess

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
Nerva was Roman emperor AD 96-98

explanation.surface: A list of Roman deities and rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Old-fashioned queen is not commonly spoken

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: A queen whose speech is not that of ordinary folk seems dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: quaint means attractively old-fashioned.

clue.text: Publish without permission page with cross

parts.note: cross means angry, irate

explanation.surface: A writer is angry about a page being used without consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to pirate a work is to reproduce it illegally.

clue.text: Some brat typically getting irritable

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spoilt child, as usual, becoming bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ratty is British informal for irritable or tetchy.

clue.text: False appearance giving trouble for all to see by holy city

parts.note: ill means trouble or misfortune
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for everyone
Sion is a variant of Zion, the holy city of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A miracle in Jerusalem is exposed as a trick for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema certificate meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an illusion is a deceptive impression.

clue.text: Man's rival regularly observed in large landmass

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A man's competitor seen across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of MANSRIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Asia is the largest continent.

clue.text: Intense expression of feeling shown by king in striking sculpture

parts.note: workers who are striking are out

indicators.note: in means the letter for king goes inside the word for sculpture

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A king's striking statue shows a powerful emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outburst is a sudden release of strong emotion.

clue.text: Old Muslim official, namely one leading queen

parts.note: viz is an abbreviation meaning namely
I is the Roman numeral one
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A historic Islamic minister, namely someone heading a queen's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a vizier was a high official in Ottoman and other Muslim states.

clue.text: Gain type suffering abuse, one from Africa

indicators.note: suffering abuse means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of advantage being mistreated, by someone from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Egyptian is a native of Egypt in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Source of shame? A car, it's backfiring!

indicators.note: backfiring means the run of letters is read back to front

parts.note: MG is a classic British make of sports car

explanation.surface: Embarrassment as a car backfires noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' sounds like engine trouble but reads A MG ITS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stigma is a mark of disgrace.
